content:
After years of waiting, Apple finally responded to significant price hikes in memory and other components — and the company isn't pulling any punches. Some increases exceed 50%, while some memory and storage upgrades have even doubled in price.

These higher prices are likely to persist for years — and may never come down…

9to5Mac readers were already skeptical about whether Apple would lower prices even after the component shortages eased. More than two-thirds of readers said they expect the price increases to be permanent.

An analyst report subsequently noted that supply chain pricing won't see any improvement until 2028, and even then only limited relief. The fact that today's extremely high pricing will remain for at least several years, and likely never return to previous levels, is now pretty well established.

If that turns out to be the case, how will you respond? Will you grit your teeth and keep buying Apple products at the same pace? Cut back on the number or frequency of Apple purchases? Or take other approaches — such as choosing lower-tier models, buying refurbished units, or waiting for a price drop before making a move?

Please take part in our poll and share your thoughts in the comments. The poll allows multiple selections, in case you plan to change your purchasing behavior in more than one way.
